post: summary: Publish now or schedule a post (all platforms)

Post content to one or more connected social accounts — TikTok, Instagram, Facebook Page, YouTube, X, LinkedIn — immediately (`schedule_type: now`), at a time (`specific_time`), or in the agent's next free calendar slot (`next_available`, default). Instagram takes 2-10 items as a carousel (optional `instagram_music`), YouTube uploads `thumbnail_url` and takes `youtube_options` (visibility, shorts, tags, ...), LinkedIn takes a PDF/PPTX/DOCX document or up to 9 images and `linkedin_options` (visibility, alt_text).

The request is validated per platform before anything is queued (media type and count, caption/title limits, required fields such as the YouTube title); a violation is a `422 platform_validation_failed` naming the platform and field. Publishing is asynchronous even for `now`: a `200` means accepted and queued. Poll `GET /schedule/post/{post_id}` for the per-platform outcome and the live `post_url`.
The agent must have connected each target platform first (GEN app → Setup → Accounts).
Any string up to 128 characters, unique per agent. A retry with the same key returns the original post (`idempotent_replay: true`) instead of creating a duplicate.

patch: summary: Edit the metadata of a post that is already live

Change a published post's metadata where the destination network supports it — today, a YouTube video's `title`, `description`, `tags` and `category_id`. `GET /schedule/platforms` names the editable fields per platform in `editable_after_publish`.

The edit is **sparse**: only the fields in the request body change. GEN reads the platform's current metadata, merges your change onto it, writes it back, and returns what the platform held afterwards — so a title you did not send is not cleared, and the same request sent twice converges on the same result rather than stacking edits.

The response is `200` with one result per platform the post went out on, each `updated`, `unsupported_after_publish`, `reauthorization_required` or `failed`. A network with no edit path is reported as `unsupported_after_publish` and nothing is touched; it is never an authentication error. A `422` means the body itself is wrong — a field the platform cannot change after publishing, or one that breaks the platform's limits.
Use `PATCH /schedule/post/{post_id}` for a post that has **not** gone out yet; that endpoint still refuses published posts.
Each YouTube update consumes 50 units of the connected channel's YouTube API quota.
